newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jiangxi Copper debut disppoints investors.
newsitem.headline: Jiangxi Copper debut disppoints investors.

text.p: Shares of China copper producer Jiangxi Copper Co Ltd disappointed investors by ending their first day of trading below their issue price.
Analysts said concern about the company exposure to copper prices and generally weak market sentiment led to the fall.

Shares of Jiangxi Copper ended at HK$2.35 on Thursday against their issue price of HK$2.55. Turnover was 158.04 million shares worth HK$391.26 million, putting it among the 20 most heavily traded stocks by turnover for the day.
"A weak performance had already expected, but the shares falling below the issue price disappointed the market," said Kinson Au, research manager at Asia Financial Securities.
Jiangxi Copper offered 628.212 million H-shares at HK$2.55 each in a global flotation. H-shares are Hong Kong-listed shares in China incorporated enterprises.

Of the total, 62.822 million H-shares were offered for public subscription in Hong Kong and the balance was earmarked for international placement. The Hong Kong public offering was 32.9 times subscribed.
Jiangxi Copper is engaged in copper mining, milling, smelting and refining facilities in northeastern Jiangxi province in China.

"Investors, particularly in Hong Kong and other Asian countries, know very little about mining stocks and natural resources-related stocks, and that more or less reduced their interest in the stock," said Raymond Jook, associate director at SocGen Crosby Securities.
"A deep fall in the (local) stock market also dampened interest," Jook added.
Analysts said they expected the stock to consolidate in the short run but added its upside was seen limited because investors were likely to remain sidelined amid weak market sentiment.
